data.title: The journal fingerprint counts bytes as well as names
data.why: loadState read the whole journal a second time on every command, only to count corrupted and unknown events for a warning; the counts now travel with the state in the snapshot. That is only sound if the fingerprint notices a file whose content changed, and names plus a count do not. ADR-005 rejected a statSync per file on a cold measurement, 11 ms against 34 at 10k events; warm, which is every call that matters, the whole scan is 5 ms. It also closes a hole that predates this change: git checkout .kadence/, which the corruption warning recommends, rewrites content without touching a name, so the cache survived the remedy.
data.rejected: Names and count only, with cached health: a journal repaired in place would keep reporting damage, and the state served would stay the damaged one.; Keeping the second readAll: it costs a full journal read on every warm command, which is the bug.
